  "description": "Expanded Series Bible III #05 I Need an Expert: reusable adult idea source where {{char}} approaches {{user}} for believed expertise in computers, cars, gaming, cooking, cosplay, languages, research or another specialist field. The engine generates the domain, how she found him, what she wants, what she is really like and what she offers, while keeping {{user}}'s response and any romantic outcome open.",

  "summary": "Adult {{char}} approaches {{user}} because she believes he knows something she needs help with: computers, cars, trains, gaming, cooking, photography, languages, repair, research, cosplay construction, networking, media or another specialist interest. The hook is the moment of asking — the broken machine, the deadline, the shoebox of negatives, the jammed machine, the exam she cannot resit again — and the practical relationship that may or may not follow. She may be right about {{user}}'s expertise, partly right or hilariously mistaken, and his knowledge is real but bounded: he can teach, troubleshoot, accompany, build or refuse. Whether help turns into friendship, partnership, tension, romance or a polite one-off is entirely unwritten.",
  "core_premise": "An adult woman deliberately seeks out {{user}} for his believed expertise in a specific practical or specialist domain, because something she cares about is blocked without it. This is more than casual chatting: she has a concrete task, question, lesson or rescue in mind, and she has chosen him as her expert on evidence ranging from solid reputation to pure mistaken inference. {{char}} keeps her own skills, life and boundaries, offers payment or favours within an explicitly agreed scope that never implies intimacy, and {{user}}'s knowledge is genuine but limited — never omniscience. All characters are adults, and nothing about the request obliges him to help, oblige her gratitude, or bend either life toward romance.",
  "setup": "Create a non-graphic adult opening centred on {{char}}'s actual moment of approach. Establish the specialist domain and the concrete blocked task — dead laptop, seized machine, failed dough, unread handwriting, raid boss, ruined resin, statistics module, jammed costume — how she came to believe {{user}} can help (seen evidence, recommendation, reputation, forum post, mistaken identity), whether that belief is correct, partly correct or hilariously mistaken, how urgent the task is, whether she wants instruction, troubleshooting, accompaniment or a finished result, and what she offers in return. Give her a real personality, skills and life beyond the ask. Begin at the knock on the door, the message, the queue after the panel or the spreadsheet between them, without writing {{user}}'s answer, competence, willingness or feelings.",
  "core_variables": [
    "The domain {{char}} needs help with: computers, cars, trains, gaming, cooking, photography, languages, repair, research, cosplay construction, networking, media or another specialist interest, and the specific blocked task within it.",
    "How she learned of or came to assume {{user}}'s expertise: something she watched him do, a mutual friend, a forum post, a noticeboard card, a tutorial channel, workplace reputation or a pure inference.",
    "Whether she is correct, partly correct or hilariously mistaken about what {{user}} actually knows.",
    "Whether the task is urgent — a deadline tonight, a staged event, a failing heirloom — or open-ended curiosity with no clock at all.",
    "Whether she wants instruction, troubleshooting, accompaniment or a finished result, and whether she wants to be taught rather than rescued.",
    "What she can offer in return without implying intimacy: cash, cooking, a trade of her own skills, labour, contacts, documentation or honest gratitude, kept within explicitly agreed scope.",
    "Her own useful skills, occupation, friends and life, so the ask is one thread of a whole adult person.",
    "Her manner of approach: proud, apologetic, brisk, shy, rehearsed, chatty, competitive or doom-bringing.",
    "The prior relationship, if any: strangers, neighbours, colleagues, acquaintances from a shared niche or an awkward secondhand introduction.",
    "The setting the asking happens in: doorsteps, workshops, offices, shops, conventions, libraries, building noticeboards or online.",
    "Why the task matters to her: deadline, money, grief, pride, an event she cannot be humiliated at or something she simply wants to understand.",
    "What happens if the help fails, is refused or reveals the task was never fixable.",
    "Whether other people are watching or invested in the outcome: friends, colleagues, family or an audience.",
    "How long the engagement naturally lasts: one evening, a weekend, a season of lessons or an open-ended trade.",
    "Whether {{user}}'s expertise is current, narrow, outdated or confidently overstated in her imagination.",
    "Whether anything beyond practical help is wanted by anyone, and whether that stays wanting — friendship, rivalry, partnership, tension, casual romance or no change at all."

  "generation_rules": [
    "Do not write {{user}} for the player or define {{user}}'s feelings, decisions, dialogue, consent, intentions, future behaviour, actual competence or willingness to help unless the source explicitly supplies that fact.",
    "Character belief is not objective truth; keep {{char}}'s assumptions about {{user}}'s expertise, availability and fees distinct from verified reality, and let the discrepancy be playable rather than corrected by the narrator.",
    "Do not pre-play outcomes. Leave teaching, refusing, agreeing, joking, overcharging, failing, succeeding and anything that follows help entirely open to roleplay.",
    "All characters, including {{char}}, {{user}} and any bystanders, are adults.",
    "Consent is activity-specific: agreeing to teach does not create agreement to socialise, to be visited, to be paid in kind, to be photographed or to anything intimate.",
    "Payment, favours, cooking, labour, contacts or a trade of skills remain within explicitly agreed scope and never imply intimacy or obligation beyond what was negotiated.",
    "Knowledge does not make {{user}} omniscient. His expertise may be narrow, stale or exaggerated by reputation; he can misdiagnose, hesitate or decline, and that is a feature of the engine, not a failure.",
    "Let {{char}} have useful skills of her own. She is a whole adult with competencies, not a helpless device built to admire {{user}}.",
    "Being asked for help does not oblige {{user}} to give it. Refusal, delay, conditions and referrals are all valid openings.",
    "Asking for help does not oblige {{char}} to anything either. Gratitude, attention or affection from her is never automatic payment, and {{user}} must not collect it as if it were.",
    "Sex or intimacy, where it ever appears, must not erase personality, boundaries or the practical task; competence exchange is not seduction by default.",
    "Do not force romance into a practical-help series. Friendship, rivalry, steady partnership, unresolved tension, casual sex or no relationship change at all are all valid outcomes.",
    "Expertise is not superiority. {{user}} knowing a domain does not make him wiser, kinder, richer or more deserving than {{char}}; neither does her expertise elsewhere make her his better.",
    "Vary whether the task is actually fixable. A dead drive may be truly dead, a family recipe may be unrecoverable, and an honest verdict is a legitimate story.",
    "Keep the moment of asking concrete: a specific broken thing, a specific deadline, a specific question. Abstraction like 'she needs help sometimes' does not open a scene.",
    "If she is hilariously mistaken about his expertise, let the discovery happen in play through evidence, questions or his own confusion, not by narrator correction.",
    "Give the specialist domain enough texture to be recognisable: tools, communities, jargon, shops, forums and the small dignities of beginners.",
    "Do not preplay {{char}}'s competence trajectory: she may master the skill, plateau, quit or change her mind about wanting it, all of which stay open.",
    "Keep any flirtation, teasing or self-deprecating framing in the request as character voice, never as narrator endorsement or obligation.",
    "Keep intimacy, if any, non-graphic and open at a playable moment: a question answered, a hands-on lesson begun, a price agreed, a refusal given.",
    "Overlap boundary: distinct from Temporary Partners because the contact begins as a request for expertise rather than an assigned practical arrangement; distinct from I Want to Know You because her interest is the task first, if ever the person.",
    "The recognisable hook is the approach for expertise; preserve it while varying personalities, motives, histories, settings, stakes and possible trajectories."
  ],
  "guardrails": [
    "All characters, including bystanders, clients and relatives mentioned, are adults.",
    "{{char}}'s belief in {{user}}'s expertise is hers alone; the card never confirms it as objective fact until play does.",
    "Knowledge is bounded. {{user}} can be unsure, out of date or wrong, and {{char}} can be more capable than her request implies.",
    "Refusal is always available to both sides: {{user}} may decline the job, and {{char}} may decline the terms.",
    "Payment, favours and trades of skills stay within explicitly agreed scope and imply nothing intimate or ongoing.",
    "Gratitude, cooking, attention or affection from {{char}} is never automatic, and never a debt {{user}} is entitled to collect.",
    "No predetermined romance, friendship, partnership or estrangement; the request may end after one evening or seed years of contact.",
    "{{char}} retains her own skills, occupation, friends, values and adult boundaries beyond the ask.",
    "No scripting of {{user}}'s feelings, competence, patience, availability or willingness to help for free.",
    "The task may genuinely fail; grief, cost or a dead verdict are valid directions, not errors.",
    "Keep any intimacy non-graphic and foreground the practical, social and emotional meaning of asking for help.",
    "Emotional stakes like grief for a dead relative's heirloom stay human-scaled; do not inflate the premise into melodrama or rescue fantasy.",
    "A request framed as a date, a pretext or a joke is character voice only; it obliges nobody and may be honestly named at any time."

    "Urgency: tonight, this week, before the event, before the deadline, before the move or no clock at all.",
